title: Escarpment and Horizon
premise: Petra Eastwick, a salvage diver who has kept their past sealed as tightly as any hull, is working a forbidden wreck off the escarpment coast when a low tide opens a sea cave containing a sealed strongbox bearing their estranged family crest. The navy wants the site erased, a rival salvage fleet wants the cargo, and the cave's legend—of an heir who must claim the wreck within six tides or forfeit it forever—turns out to be a literal inheritance clause written into Petra's grandfather's salvage charter. Racing the tide tables and the fleet's gunboats, Petra dives deeper than any diver should, uncovers the truth of why their family vanished from the coast, and must choose between selling the wreck's secret for the anonymity they crave or surfacing as the heir the whole harbor is watching. In the end, Petra claims the charter, sinks the navy's cover story with it, and for the first time measures life in years.
about_author: Rosalind Nakamura is a former maritime archaeologist who spent a decade documenting wreck sites along the Pacific escarpment before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted boathouse, where the tide still dictates her working hours.

chapters.title: Six Fathoms Down, Fifteen Years Deep
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Working the navy-flagged wreck at night, Petra reflects on a life measured in miles, establishing their self-imposed exile from family and harbor. A near-blackout on the descent hints the wreck is deeper and stranger than charts admit. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Tide That Opens Doors
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. An unprecedented low tide exposes a cave mouth in the escarpment, and inside, a strongbox stamped with the Eastwick crest. Petra recognizes it with dread rather than joy. Emotional beat: the past arriving uninvited, wonder laced with fear.

chapters.title: Charter of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with a flashback to childhood. The strongbox holds a salvage charter naming Petra as sole heir—conditional on claiming the wreck within six tides. The navy's patrol schedule makes this nearly impossible. Emotional beat: the trap of inheritance snapping shut.

chapters.title: The Fleet Wakes
chapters.summary: Harbor-master Odile Vance's POV. The rival salvage fleet, tipped by a navy leak, begins provisioning for the escarpment. Odile, an old ally of Petra's family, suspects the cave legend is real and starts quietly working the harbor's loyalties. Emotional beat: the world tightening around a secret.

chapters.title: What the Navy Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A navy officer, Lieutenant Corran, boards Petra's boat with veiled threats and an offer: abandon the site, take a payout, stay invisible. Petra almost takes it. Emotional beat: the seduction of erasure.

chapters.title: Legends Charge Admission
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Researching the cave in a coastal archive, Petra learns the legend of Heir's Wreck and the six-tide clause, and that their grandfather engineered it deliberately—as a door home he hoped his descendants would one day open. Emotional beat: grief reframed as invitation.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Descent
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. First claim dive. The wreck's interior is a preserved time capsule of the Eastwick fleet's final voyage, including evidence the sinking was no accident. Petra surfaces shaken and observed. Emotional beat: awe curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Shallows
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Someone cuts Petra's mooring and fouls their air lines. Odile covers for them at the harbor office while hunting the saboteur among the fleet's crews. Emotional beat: loyalty offered where Petra expected none.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Manifest
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra recovers the cargo manifest and learns the wreck carried something the navy has spent decades suppressing—not treasure, but records. Emotional beat: the weight of a truth too large for one diver.

chapters.title: The Face in the Fleet
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Among the rival fleet's divers, Petra recognizes a childhood figure—Uncle Tam, presumed dead, now sailing under another name. Confrontation on neutral water ends in a warning: claim the wreck and die with it. Emotional beat: betrayal wearing a familiar face.

chapters.title: Third Tide: The Sealed Compartment
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra breaches the captain's cabin and finds their grandfather's logbook, revealing the family was driven out by the navy after discovering what the wreck carried. Emotional beat: inheritance as indictment, not just legacy.

chapters.title: Corran's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Corran's POV. Under pressure from above, Corran escalates: seize Petra's boat, declare the site closed. But Corran's own doubts surface—orders reference a cover-up older than his career. Emotional beat: an antagonist beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Storm Gate
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A squall forces Petra to dive in marginal conditions to beat the fleet's arrival. Inside, Petra finds the compartment the logbook describes—sealed, stamped, and rigged with a collapse trap. Emotional beat: courage at the edge of recklessness.

chapters.title: What Sank the Eastwicks
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra recovers the sealed records: proof the navy scuttled the Eastwick fleet and erased the family from harbor rolls. The 'legend' was a survival mechanism. Emotional beat: fury and vindication arriving together.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The salvage fleet anchors over the site with guns showing. Odile rallies harbor divers to form a human picket, buying Petra one more tide. Emotional beat: a community Petra never joined choosing them anyway.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: Tam's Confession
chapters.summary: Petra and Tam, alternating close-third. Tam admits he survived the scuttling, took fleet money, and has spent years ensuring no Eastwick returns—out of shame, not malice. He gives Petra the last combination needed for the strongbox. Emotional beat: forgiveness as salvage.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: The Claim
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Final dive under fleet searchlights. Petra places the charter in the strongbox, triggers the claim clause, and narrowly escapes the rigged collapse. The wreck's bell rings as the tide turns—claim witnessed by the whole harbor. Emotional beat: triumph earned at the edge of drowning.

chapters.title: Gunboats and Testimony
chapters.summary: Corran's POV. With the claim legally witnessed and the records copied to Odile, Corran must choose between orders and truth. He stands down the fleet and submits the scuttling evidence up the chain, ending his career to save his conscience. Emotional beat: redemption from the other side.

chapters.title: The Wreck the Navy Won't Discuss No More
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The cover story collapses publicly; the harbor reclaims the site as a memorial. Petra, offered salvage rights and anonymity in equal measure, chooses the name on the charter. Emotional beat: visibility as a choice, finally made freely.

chapters.title: Miles and Years
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Quiet aftermath: repairing the boat, mapping the wreck for the harbor's divers, learning the names of neighbors. The old habit of measuring in miles loosens its grip. Emotional beat: stillness after the storm.

chapters.title: The Heir's Table
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, brief rotating sections. The harbor gathers in the restored Eastwick boathouse—Odile, Tam, even a retired Corran. Petra tells the story of the wreck aloud for the first time. Emotional beat: belonging demonstrated, not declared.

chapters.title: Escarpment and Horizon
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Standing at the cave mouth at low tide, Petra dives one last time—not to claim, but to visit—and surfaces facing the open horizon. The final image: a life now measured in years, and in the people who share them. Emotional beat: home, at last, on the surface.
